reviews.author: Skip Watson
reviews.title: Spectacular, Get Here Early
reviews.text: Spent 3 nights here in a 35' TT. Got here on a Thurs and 1 site we could have squeezed into with a shoehorn, and only one other site we were fairly comfortable in...cozy, but comfortable. LOTS of tents and car campers...many of those in the bigger sites for RVs. Very family friendly and dog friendly...not a criticism since I'm a grandpa of 9 and have been a dog dad most of my 75 years. Very easy beach access and easy access (though an hour + away) to most of the western side of the park (that's why you're here, right?). VERY loosely monitored, if at all. Never saw a ranger and there's a "host" parked in the host spot, but had an "off duty" sign in front all 3 days. Supposed to be "no picnic table, no parking", but we saw many people cram into any bare spot they could find and nobody chased them away. Could be mistaken for a homeless encampment, but everyone was very chill and respectful of others. Flush toilets, no sinks. 2 bars AT&T. Good solar and Starlink. $20/$10 Sr pass

reviews.author: Don Oakland
reviews.title: Great Place!
reviews.text: One of those places where if you get one of the great places you love it. If you show up late in the dark on a weekend you get leftovers. Not a lot of BIG stuff in here but a 30 ft. Class C is kind of normal and all of the Class B vans. Planned on 4 nights might stay for 6. And it rains, but you knew that right?

reviews.author: Laz Gutierrez
reviews.title: Surprise
reviews.text: This was our first family camping event in WA and although we were aiming for Kalalouch Campsite (it was full upon our arrival), we discovered that South Beach was an even better fit for our family. You are steps away from the beach and the sea breeze and waves just put you to sleep. The amazing sunset just makes it for some amazing memories. Our kids truly enjoyed their time there and Keith (the big guy in charge) was a friendly face with great service and stories. Close to the HOH Rainforest, Big cedar tree, Tree of life, Ruby beach and more. Highly recommend! No hookups but the bathrooms are cleaned and spacious sites we had #19 and it was perfect for our 20x20 tent.

reviews.author: Ronzoni
reviews.title: Love This Place
reviews.text: Been coming here for 9 years, always try to get site 47. They provide absolutely nothing so bring what you need. The views are great and it is so peaceful. Saw seals and whales today. They are catching perch in the surf and this site has its very own path down to the beach. Scatter my ashes here

reviews.author: RW&DKBaker
reviews.title: Can't Beat View
reviews.text: Beautiful spot with beautiful Pacific ocean views, nice beach, no electric, tables and fire pits/bbq at each of the 56 sites.

reviews.author: Plonski
reviews.text: Very basic on the ocean but not very pretty and mud. Lot of big rigs snug the ocean and block view. Go north a little way and find some beauty

reviews.author: gfs
reviews.title: Very Basic
reviews.text: But great spots overlooking the ocean. We plan to come again if ever in the area again. Very relaxing.

reviews.author: Joshua Barr
reviews.title: Beautiful view. Whales. Flush toilets.
reviews.text: Beautiful view. Whales. Flush toilets. A few sites available on the weekdays at mid morning in the shoulder season if your rig isn't 70 feet long. Good cell signal. Water and dump available at the Kalaloch campground to the north.

reviews.author: MTtrippers
reviews.title: Took a chance to get a spot at this site and lucked out
reviews.text: Took a chance to get a spot at this site and lucked out- got site 29 at the end of the campground, which had open space for doggos. Were able to level our rig with a few blocks. The sites were clean and every one had a great view of the ocean. Cost was $10 with senior pass. Bathroom was clean. No water available, so plan ahead! Paths to beach are a bit of a challenge (lots of logs to climb over), but you can walk for miles of undeveloped sand and rocky beaches at low tide. I'd definitely stay again!

reviews.author: camper-898145
reviews.text: May 12; closed. This app said it was opened.

reviews.author: camper-828321
reviews.text: Arrived about 2pm on Sunday, October 1st. Tons of open spaces. We chose one right on the bluff. We have a 22' TT and it needed little leveling in spot 30. Saw some larger class As too. Self register with debit or Credit card. Fire ring and picnic table at each site. Trash and clean restrooms with flush toilets no sink. Pretty quiet the 2 nights we were there with maybe 8 sites occupied. Closes 10/10/23

reviews.author: llauer
reviews.text: This is a great spot with easy beach access. There are no reservations and it fills up by early afternoon, so get here early. Bathrooms are clean and stocked. There is no water, so come prepared.

reviews.author: Sparklers
reviews.text: We arrived on the Friday before 4th of July at noon and got the next to the last site. As others have said, it's not private but the views and sound of the surf make up for it. We had no clouds or rain for 3 days so it got a bit dusty for the PNW. Closest diesel and propane over 45 minutes away, so come prepared. Gas available at Queets 5 miles away. Check with the host and the board at the bathrooms to verify which sites are open.

reviews.author: camp-shanebarzilla
reviews.text: There are definitely toilets but no sinks. I am not sure how the other reviewer missed them since you register literally at the toilet! No other amenities except that it is across the street from the Tsunami evacuation route. Listed on the NPS website as 21-foot sites with a few for 35 feet, well there were either vans, tent campers with lots of tents, or huge rigs. Class As, large 5th wheels, all that do not really have problems because there are no site markings except the picnic tables... so it does really start to look like an extremely busy highway gravel rest area next to the ocean. If every single neighbor would not have been using generators nonstop this would have been a great site. Note that high tides can come all the way up to the rocks and beyond so use caution when tide is coming in and check out the tide chart posted by the toilets.

reviews.author: Grace
reviews.title: Hidden Gem by the Ocean
reviews.text: South Beach campground is one of those hidden gems I wish I had gotten to spend more time at. It seems at first glance like overflow camping from Mora, but if I'm ever in the area again I'll choose this site over that in a heartbeat. There isn't much privacy, and there are only about twenty sites, but don't let that dissuade you. The sunsets are spectacular, the stars at night even more so, and the beach is only a few steps away the entire time.

reviews.author: Al's A
reviews.text: South Beach Campground is located in the Olympic National Park. The campground is well maintained for tent and RV camping. No running water and electricity. Each camp site has a beautiful view of the ocean. The cost per night is $20.00. I highly recommend camping at South Beach Campground.

reviews.author: Dustin W
reviews.title: A Favorite Family Camping Spot by the Ocean
reviews.text: Our family loved camping at South Beach Campground! It quickly became one of our favorite places to camp—mostly because of its unbeatable proximity to the beach. There's nothing quite like falling asleep to the sound of crashing waves and waking up to stunning ocean views just steps from your site. We especially enjoyed sitting at our campsite watching sea otters playfully swim by and pods of porpoises glide through the surf. It felt like we had a front-row seat to the wonders of the Pacific Ocean. That said, expectations are everything. This campground is basically a large, open parking lot on the edge of a bluff overlooking the water. There are no hookups, and little to no privacy between sites. There is a set of flush toilets, but they can be smelly, and there are no sinks or running water available for campers. We had to drive several miles up the road to another campground to fill our water containers—so come prepared.
